# Additional root evidence — withheld until both original angles freeze

The earlier exact query for ngo shes was empty; the actual complete source
word is ngo shes pa. Broader original lookup now yields full HGM22564, whose
entire gloss is recognize. This positive evidence must be confronted, not
misreported as glossary absence. All fields/raw original are preserved in
root-broader-lexical-context.json, along with the second unglossed related row.

The sgro 'dogs prefix query returns9 entries,2 HGM-positive (3269,22477).
Neither the exact query nor this prefix inventory supplies a full sgro 'dogs
chod pa headword. Four corpus rows contain sgro 'dogs chod: C05:261/C15:406/
C16:837 and EM:918. EM's complete local rendering includes having threshed out
the ideas through learning and contemplation; it is a semantic comparator,
not permission to compose those words inC05. C05's actual analyze remains the
only English to select from locally. Preserve whether sgro 'dogs contributes
within a complete recast or is distributed; a positive implying glossary
variant does not license the rhetorical implying occurrence from thal framing.
The root does not preselect a final depth/extent here.

The broader ngo shes corpus query returns37 complete rows, including recognizing,
telling, acquaintance and dream-recognition contexts. All original fields and
query parameters/counts are saved; variation does not imply that every sense is
interchangeable. The local reciprocal recognition still requires correct agent/
object roles and actual source ranges. No erratum proposed by these queries.
Full HGM/reference fields for material3269/22477/22564 and all resulting original
Tibetan/English contexts were read. Only measured digital relations are asserted.

# Root comparison after both original angles froze

Both originals remain immutable. Tibetan has 27/38/17 spans, English
32/45/18. All six actual canonical runs exited zero with empty stderr and
byte-identical bodies. Root resolved all 177 spans with the actual generator.
Root checked 111 Tibetan frozen files and 65 English frozen files, their actual
governing and archive pins, and the English original's 47 saved SQL queries.
These checks establish identity and mechanics, not semantic approval.

Read both complete originals, root-review-targets.md, its addendum, and the
complete root-broader-lexical-context.json. The following comparisons are
review targets, not preselected decisions:

- 259: Tibetan groups kho na re with Someone may answer; English splits kho /
  Someone and na re / claim. Determine the actual reporting relation and
  defensible lexical units; neither a dictionary variant nor angle agreement
  alone establishes local boundaries.
- 259: English gnyis / two types versus Tibetan two needs explicit treatment
  of the supplied classifier. Both angles split bzang / good and ngan / bad;
  confront the positive whole bzang ngan entry and the source's two karma
  cases, rather than silently discarding established compound coverage.
- 259–260: dbang versus dbang gis / forces; yin copulas at d5 versus d6;
  259 sogs / like (d6) versus something like (d5). State each actual licensor
  and any proposed head allowance. A grammatical depth must not hide a false
  relation and a shallow lexical match must not discard useful true scope.
- English adds immediate members to sensory consciousnesses, pus/blood,
  original position and definite conclusion. Check each member's own source
  exponent, uniqueness and immediate-parent containment; do not simply prefer
  the higher span count.
- 260: English's report correctly counts four tshad ma occurrences, but the
  frozen spec note says "all three original tshad ma formulations" before
  listing the initial valid perception and tactile/auditory/visual valid.
  Preserve the erroneous original wording as review history and correct the
  final note's measured count. Do not alter the original proposal freeze.
- 260: Tibetan includes yin / is in mi ma yin pa while English omits it.
  Tibetan khyod / your (d5) versus English khyod kyi / your (d3) needs actual
  phrase and possessive scope. The first negative contraction must resolve
  to the first n't in wouldn't, with the exact subword flag preserved.
- 260–261: narrow thal / implying (d6) versus the complete rhetorical
  consequence questions (d3) needs a reasoned treatment of supplied address,
  auxiliaries, then and that. Full phrase recasts are allowed only when the
  whole source relation licenses the entire selected English.
- 261: both proposals select chod pa / analyze and omit sgro 'dogs. Confront
  the broader full-phrase EM:918 comparator and actual local source before
  accepting that agreement. Record omitted/distributed content honestly;
  do not redirect it to thal's implying or manufacture a null.

Preserve all optional original span keys as well as the exact original IDs,
depths, strings and canonical Tibetan/English ranges in exhaustive dispositions.
Record all final ordered tuples, omissions and five refutation grounds. There
is no request to manufacture errata or extend beyond these three segments.

full_source.acip: 'O NA MI'I MIG SHES TSAD MA MA YIN PAR THAL, MI LAS 'BRING PO'I DBANG GIS CHUR MTHONG BA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, GZHAN YANG , MI MA YIN PA'I 'GRO BA'I RGYUD LA LUS SHES TSAD MA DANG , NYAN SHES TSAD MA YANG MED PAR THAL, DE'I RGYUD LA MIG SHES TSAD MA MED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, KHYOD KYI RTZA BA'I DAM BCA' 'THAD PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA,
full_source.wylie: 'o na mi'i mig shes tshad ma ma yin par thal, mi las 'bring po'i dbang gis chur mthong ba tsam yin pa'i phyir, gzhan yang , mi ma yin pa'i 'gro ba'i rgyud la lus shes tshad ma dang , nyan shes tshad ma yang med par thal, de'i rgyud la mig shes tshad ma med pa'i phyir, der thal, khyod kyi rtsa ba'i dam bca' 'thad pa'i phyir, 'dod na
full_source.english: Well then, according to you, the visual consciousness of the human wouldn't be valid perception either. Because isn't it true that the human sees the water only because his karma (which in this case is halfway between the good and the bad just mentioned) forces him to? Moreover, aren't you implying then that there is no such thing as a valid tactile consciousness, or a valid auditory consciousness, in the mental stream of any being who is not a human? Because aren't you saying that there's no such thing as a valid visual consciousness in the mental stream of any such being? Certainly you are, for you believe your original position to be correct. And suppose now that you do agree that such beings can have no such valid consciousnesses.
